narrativeProgression.description: The interviewer introduces Michael Dale from Kaltura.
The interviewer asks Dale to explain what Kaltura is.
The interviewer asks Dale who is using Kaltura.
The interviewer points out that the video area is traditionally very patent-encumbered.
The interviewer notes that Kaltura is open source, which means that the code is publicly available.
Dale encourages viewers to submit pull requests to the Kaltura project.
The interviewer mentions that there is a rumor that Kaltura has a conference and some competitions coming up.
Dale confirms that Kaltura Connect is coming up and says that his colleague Zohar will tell the viewers all about it.
Zohar Babin from Kaltura joins the conversation.
The interviewer asks Babin to tell the viewers about the competitions and the conference.
Babin gives the dates and location of Kaltura Connect and says that it is one of the most exciting conferences in the world for people who care about online video and the future of media.
Babin announces the three contests that will be held at Kaltura Connect.
Babin encourages viewers to check out Kaltura's website and GitHub page.

That basically means if you want to be able to create your own YouTube, that's something that Calchura enables to make.
It's a complete open source stack for transcoding, ingestion, analytics, monetization, distribution.
Okay, it's a full platform for doing everything you want to do with online video today.
And so who is using this? Who that we would have heard of was using this?

We have quite a few customers ranging from large media companies like Disney and HBO to a lot of educational institutions using it as a sort of like a campus YouTube in order to deliver their lectures and online content to their students.
So now this is in the video area which is traditionally very patent-encumbered. Codex are a blood bath. So, you're doing all this open source.
Is it real open source or is it open source as long as swing tag on the outside?
Well, I mean, so our primary offering sort of a SaaS service, software service, where we sort of manage all the licensing requirements.

And then we also sort of have an on-premise installation where we also sort of license to the appropriate licensing for the Codex and then sell it similar to Goontoo with media extensions or any fluendo also with selling extensions to G-streamers that enabled you to encode and decode.

Some of the patented codex. We play that same game as well. But we also do web-m and we also try to support codex and we've worked with the Wikimedia Foundation on promoting free and open codex for quite some time.
Right, it's also something more entwined.
So, this is all open source. That means it's in some repository somewhere that the viewers can go to and check stuff out.

Check us out on GitHub slash CalTurret. We got all our repositories up there. We just recently moved our entire server package onto GitHub so you can actually use very close to exactly what's being offered on our SaaS service and follow along our entire development and taking place in public.
It's a great way to get the inside scoop on a giant production platform of online video distribution.
And how is that all licensed?

We use the AGPL for our content and that's just to enable other companies that use it since it's primarily an online service that would enable us to ensure that everybody is able to benefit when some other company is using the code and creating new experiences with it and comes back to the community.
So, you'd like people to get involved in that project and make pull requests?
Yes, please do. We love pull requests.

We love, yeah, there's a great repository. There you can check it out. There's player.calTurret.com, sort of has our entire front-end platform as sort of a visible feature hub there and then the back-end platform is also available to check it out and check it out locally.

So, CalTurret Connect is happening on September 30th and October 1st in New York, New York City.

I think it's one of the most exciting conferences in the world. If you care about online video, if you cared about the future of media in general, you're going to meet there a lot of experts from education field, from enterprises, from media and entertainment companies like publishers and broadcasters.

Along with CalTurret Connect, we're announcing three different contests actually. One is a contested for the future of online video.
